tasks.title: Make PowerShell gate processes UTF-8
tasks.goal: Set UTF-8 encodings inside every pwsh and powershell process that the shared gate runner starts. This gives gates and checks correct native-input and native-output decoding without changing their recorded commands or exit codes.

references.why: P-5 requires the setup to remain inside the plan's PowerShell gate shell and to change no machine-wide state.
Defines GateCommand as the one gate runner and requires the gate to remain outside implementation-owned tests.
GateArgs and GateCommand are the implementation surface used by gates, checks, task gate, and release commands.

acceptance: GateCommand configures [Console]::OutputEncoding, [Console]::InputEncoding, and $OutputEncoding as BOM-free UTF-8 before the recorded command runs for both pwsh and powershell, while attempting setup failures silently and continuing to the recorded command.
The shared runner preserves the recorded command's stdout, stderr, and exit code; an exit 3 remains 3 and the setup itself prints nothing.

Native git output containing café reaches a PowerShell Select-String assertion intact, and café sent through a PowerShell pipeline to git hash-object has the expected UTF-8 bytes and platform line ending.
The invocation arguments for sh, bash, and cmd are unchanged, and shown, recorded, or logged gate command text contains only the recorded command, never the encoding setup.

Committed tests run by the go check cover native output, native stdin, emitted bytes, all three BOM-free encodings, setup silence, exit-code preservation, and the unchanged non-PowerShell argument lists; the planner-owned oracle is not used as that test suite.

tasks.title: Document UTF-8 behavior for PowerShell users
tasks.goal: Explain where vloop supplies UTF-8 and where an interactive PowerShell terminal still needs profile setup. The distinction prevents the new runner behavior from being mistaken for a machine-wide encoding change.

references.why: The Mixed teams section is the required location for the vloop-versus-terminal UTF-8 explanation and profile line.
Gates and the gate shell constrains how the documentation describes the shell invocation.

acceptance: The Mixed teams section says vloop runs pwsh gates and checks with UTF-8 input and output so native tool output remains correct on Windows.
The paragraph distinguishes vloop's behavior from a person's own PowerShell terminal and includes the exact profile line [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new().
The paragraph explains that the profile line makes vloop run output remain correct through Tee-Object and similar terminal pipes, without claiming that vloop changes the profile or machine code page.

tasks.title: Verify PowerShell UTF-8 through the built CLI
tasks.goal: Prove the completed runner and documentation together through the built vloop CLI in an isolated repository. This catches integration breaks that either task's focused oracle could miss.

references.why: The close gate must exercise the same shared gate runner used by task gate and must remain an independent planner-owned oracle.
The integration assertions target GateCommand's public gate-running behavior without changing recorded commands.

acceptance: A built CLI in a temporary git repository runs the worked example's native git read and café output gates successfully and reports the exit-3 gate as a failure while vloop task gate itself exits 1.
vloop task show prints each recorded verify command unchanged, including the café assertion, and never prints the implementation's encoding setup.
The close gate runs the T1 and T2 oracles together, uses only temporary repositories and build outputs, and leaves the repository tree unchanged.
